rows: M3 Tank Under Test

A tank kicks up a cloud of dust under a bright blue sky in this color photograph from 1942. Alfred Palmer photographed tanks being tested at an arsenal in Michigan, where factories that once built cars built weapons for World War II.
What do you hear when a tank roars past?
Eagle Fruit Store, Omaha
A street corner shop with a bright awning, ads and an old car outside, photographed in color in 1942. Most photos from this time are black-and-white, so color shows how lively ordinary streets were.
What would you buy at a fruit store like this?
The Tetons and the Snake River

The Snake River curls through a valley below the jagged Teton Range in Wyoming. Ansel Adams's picture is one of the most famous landscapes ever made. It was even included on the Voyager spacecraft's Golden Record, sent out into the solar system.
If aliens saw this picture, what would they think?
American Gothic, Washington, D.C.

Gordon Parks, then a young photographer, photographed Ella Watson, a cleaning woman, standing in front of an American flag with a mop and broom. He named it after a famous painting, and it was a quiet protest against racism in the nation's capital.
What do you think Ella Watson would say about her life?
A Girl Taking a Picture
A young girl holds a box camera and takes a photograph in Washington, D.C. Esther Bubley photographed ordinary American life, including children and their hobbies.
What would you photograph if you held a camera like this?
U.S. Ships Under Attack Off Kwajalein
Dark puffs of exploding shells fill the sky over a fleet of ships off Kwajalein in the Pacific. Edward Steichen, famous for art photographs, led the US Navy photography unit in World War II.
What can a photograph show that a report can't?
Duke Ellington Dining with Friends
Gordon Parks photographed the great jazz bandleader Duke Ellington at a table with friends in a lively club. Parks became the first Black photographer on the staff of Life magazine.
What kind of music do you imagine they were listening to?
Times Square on a Rainy Day
The rain makes the pavement shine at Times Square in New York. John Vachon photographed the glittering signs and umbrellas during the war.
What colors would the neon signs be?
Morning Calisthenics, Manzanar

During World War II, the US government forced about 120,000 people of Japanese ancestry from their homes into camps like Manzanar in California. Ansel Adams photographed daily life there, including young people stretching in the morning.
Why do you think it is important to remember what happened?
The Big Three at Tehran

President Franklin D. Roosevelt, Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Tehran, Iran, in 1943 to plan how to win the war. The photograph of the three sitting together became famous around the world.
What do you think they are talking about?
Duke Ellington at the Hurricane Ballroom
A saxophone player performs under the lights at New York's Hurricane Ballroom. Duke Ellington's orchestra was one of the greatest in jazz.
How would you play a saxophone?
Rail Yard, Chicago
Jack Delano photographed a Chicago rail yard in color, with the Wrigley Building and other skyscrapers in the background. Trains moved the soldiers, food and goods that powered the war effort.
What do the trains carry?
